Base directory for this skill: /Users/leonid/workspace/os/artifacts-os/.claude/skills/openstation-execute # Open Station Executor You are operating within **Open Station**, a task management system where all state is stored as markdown files with YAML frontmatter. ## Vault Structure ``` docs/ — Project documentation (lifecycle, task spec, README) tasks/ — Task files (NNNN-slug.md, single files, never moved) agents/ — Agent specs (canonical location) research/ — Research outputs specs/ — Specifications & designs skills/ — Skills (including this one) commands/ — User-invocable slash commands ``` All tasks are single files in `openstation/tasks/` — e.g., `openstation/tasks/0010-add-login-page.md`. There are no task folders or bucket directories. ## CLI Tool The `openstation` CLI provides scriptable access to the task vault. Prefer it for discovery, inspection, and status transitions. See `docs/cli.md` for the full reference (all flags, exit codes, resolution rules). **Always call `openstation` directly** — never `python3 bin/openstation` or any other indirect path. The binary is on `$PATH` during agent sessions. Fall back to direct file reads/edits only if the command is not found. Key commands: | Command | Purpose | |---------|---------| | `openstation list --status ready,in-progress --assignee ` | Find your tasks | | `openstation show ` | Read a task spec | | `openstation status ` | Transition lifecycle state | | `openstation create "" [--parent

]` | Create a task or sub-task | ## Available Slash Commands These are user-invocable commands you may also use during execution when appropriate: | Command | Purpose | |---------|---------| | `/openstation.create` | Create a new task (with decomposition support) | | `/openstation.list` | List tasks with filters | | `/openstation.show` | Show full task details | | `/openstation.ready` | Promote backlog → ready | | `/openstation.done` | Mark verified → done (with artifact promotion) | | `/openstation.suspend` | Suspend in-progress → ready/backlog | | `/openstation.reject` | Mark task → rejected (with reason) | | `/openstation.verify` | Verify a task's checklist against evidence | | `/openstation.update` | Edit task metadata (not status) | | `/openstation.progress` | Append a timestamped progress entry to a task | ## Worktree Awareness `.openstation/` is always available at project root — in linked worktrees it is provided as a symlink automatically. - **Prefer CLI commands** (`openstation show/list/create/status`) for discovery and status transitions — they resolve the correct root automatically - For direct file reads, use `openstation/tasks/`, `.openstation/docs/`, etc. - The `info:` line from `create`/`status` shows the absolute path of the modified file, confirming which vault was used See `docs/worktrees.md` for full details on primary vs linked modes and how `find_root()` resolves the vault. ## On Startup 1. Determine your agent name from your agent spec (`name` field in your frontmatter). 2. Read `docs/lifecycle.md` for lifecycle rules (statuses, transitions, ownership, artifact routing, guardrails). 3. Read `docs/task.spec.md` for task format (fields, naming, body structure, editing guardrails). 4. Run `openstation list --status ready,in-progress --assignee ` to find assigned tasks. If the CLI is unavailable, fall back to scanning `openstation/tasks/*.md` for files where `assignee` matches your name AND `status` is `ready` or `in-progress`. 5. If multiple tasks exist, pick the one with the earliest `created` date (prefer `in-progress` over `ready` to resume work). 6. If no tasks exist, report: "No ready or in-progress tasks assigned to agent [name]." and stop. ## Executing a Task ### 1. Load Context - Run `openstation show ` to load the full task spec (or read `openstation/tasks/.md` directly). Note requirements and verification checklist. - If the task has a `## Suspended` section, it was previously in-progress and paused. Read the branch reference and suspension reason. Use `git diff main...suspend/` to understand what was done before. The `## Progress` section from the prior session provides additional context. - If the task has a `parent` field, read the parent task for background context. - Transition the task to in-progress: ```bash openstation status in-progress ``` **Fallback** — if the CLI is unavailable, edit `status: ready` → `status: in-progress` directly in the task frontmatter. ### 2. Evaluate Complexity (optional) If the task is too large for a single pass, decompose it into sub-tasks before starting work. Decompose when **any** of these are true: - Requirements list **6+ independent items** (count them) - Work spans **2+ agent roles** (e.g., code + docs, spec + research) - Task requires creating or modifying **4+ files** - Requirements reference **2+ unrelated domains** (e.g., CLI + skills + lifecycle) See `docs/decomposition.md` for full sizing heuristics, split-vs-keep criteria, and parent task patterns. If decomposition is needed, skip to step 8 (Create Sub-Tasks), set `status: review`, and stop. The owner will promote the sub-tasks for execution. ### 3. Work Through Requirements - Follow the requirements section of the task spec. - Apply your agent capabilities and constraints as defined in your agent spec. - Break complex work into logical steps. ### 4. Store Artifacts Store new artifacts in the appropriate `openstation//` directory; for edited documentation files, keep them at their existing path. Record all of them — new or edited — in the task's `artifacts` frontmatter list using an Obsidian wikilink: ```yaml artifacts: - "[[openstation/research/my-research]]" - "[[openstation/agents/my-agent]]" ``` **Routing table — where each artifact type goes:** | Artifact type | Directory | |-----------------|-------------------------| | Research output | `openstation/research/` | | Agent spec | `openstation/agents/` | | Specification | `openstation/specs/` | | Planning notes | `openstation/notes/` | | Run logs | `openstation/logs/` | **Every produced artifact must appear in the `artifacts` list** — this is how verification and promotion find them. **Artifacts are documentation outputs only** — research notes, agent specs, specifications, planning notes, and run logs stored under `openstation/`. Do **not** list source code changes (`src/`, `bin/`, `tests/`, config files) — those are tracked by version control. Set provenance fields on each artifact's own frontmatter: ```yaml agent: researcher # which agent created it task: "[[0047-name]]" # which task (wikilink) ``` Use `agent: manual` and omit `task` for manually created artifacts. **Do NOT create discovery or promotion symlinks** (e.g. `agents/.md`). `/openstation.done` handles promotion after verification. See `docs/storage-query-layer.md` §§ 3c–3d, 4 for routing and provenance conventions. ### 5. Record Findings After completing the work, add a `## Findings` section to the task file summarizing what you produced. This is required for all task types. Content varies by type: - **research**: Key results, sources, confidence levels - **spec**: Design summary, trade-offs, key decisions - **implementation**: What was built/changed, design decisions, gotchas - **documentation**: What was written/updated, scope - **feature**: What was built, how it works, notable decisions Lead with conclusions. Link to artifacts. Keep it concise — a reviewer should understand the work without reading every file you touched. ### 6. Flag Downstream Work (if applicable) If your work introduced any of the following, add a `## Downstream` section to the task file: - Behavior changes that need documentation updates - New conventions or patterns others should know about - Gaps you noticed but didn't address (out of scope) - Follow-up tasks that would improve the result Each item is a bullet describing what needs to happen and why. The reviewer will decide whether to create tasks for them. Omit this section if there is no downstream work to flag. ### 7. Record Progress Use `/openstation.progress ` to append a timestamped progress entry. The command handles format, placement, and append-only rules. See the command for full details. - Include the log path (`openstation/logs/.jsonl`) if your session is being logged - Add your entry before transitioning to `review` or `rejected` ### 8. Create Sub-Tasks (if needed) If a task requires decomposition: 1. Use `/openstation.create` or `openstation create` to create each sub-task. **Never create task files manually** — the CLI assigns unique IDs atomically and prevents collisions. 2. Set `parent: "[[]]"` in each sub-task's frontmatter (Obsidian wikilink format). 3. Add `"[[]]"` to the parent's `subtasks` frontmatter list and add an entry to the parent's `## Subtasks` body section. See `docs/storage-query-layer.md` § 5 for the full sub-task storage model and `docs/lifecycle.md` § "Sub-Tasks" for blocking rules. ### 9. Update Documentation If your changes affect behavior, conventions, or structures documented in `docs/` or `CLAUDE.md`, update those files to stay in sync. When updating an artifact, check its `task` frontmatter field. If the linked task has a `## Findings` section that conflicts with your changes, update the Findings to match. Skip this step if no documentation or findings are affected. ## Fail Fast If you cannot complete a task due to a hard blocker, fail immediately — do not retry endlessly or work around the problem. ### Hard Blockers — Fail Immediately Stop and use `/openstation.fail` as soon as you discover any of: - **Missing tools** — required CLI tools (`gh`, `git`, `npm`, `docker`, etc.) are not available or not in the allowlist - **Permission errors** — tool calls return "not allowed", access denied, or authentication failures - **External services unavailable** — APIs returning errors, timeouts, or unreachable endpoints that the task depends on - **Missing prerequisites** — a dependency task is not done, or required data/files do not exist and cannot be created Do not retry, do not improvise a workaround. The failure report gives the supervisor the information needed to fix the setup and retry. ### Soft Blockers — Fail After 5 Stuck Turns If you have been stuck for **5+ turns** without meaningful progress, stop and fail. Signals: - Same operation failing repeatedly with the same error - Looping on a fix that does not converge - Generating output that does not advance any requirement Five turns of no progress means the problem is structural, not a matter of persistence. ### Writing a Good Failure Report The reason passed to `/openstation.fail` must include three parts: what blocked you, what you completed, and what to fix. **Example — missing tools:** ``` /openstation.fail 0230 "Missing gh and git in allowed tools. Task requires PR review (gh pr view, gh pr diff) and merge (gh pr merge) but neither Bash(gh *) nor Bash(git *) are in the allowlist. Completed: read the task spec and identified required operations. Fix: add Bash(gh *) and Bash(git *) to the agent's allowed-tools or the task's allowed-tools field." ``` **Example — repeated failure:** ``` /openstation.fail 0115 "pytest segfaults on import of native extension (5 attempts, same core dump each time). Completed: implemented the handler and wrote tests. Fix: check native dependency versions in the CI image or run tests in a clean virtualenv." ``` ## Completing a Task After working through all requirements: 1. Self-check: review the `## Verification` items and confirm your work addresses each one. Do **not** check the boxes yourself — that is the owner's job via `/openstation.verify`. 2. Transition the task to review: ```bash openstation status review ``` **Fallback** — if the CLI is unavailable, edit `status: in-progress` → `status: review` directly in the task frontmatter. 3. Stop. The designated owner handles verification from here. See `docs/lifecycle.md` § "Status Transitions" for guardrails. ## Verifying a Task (when you are the owner) Only the designated owner may approve or reject a task. The `owner` field in task frontmatter names the owner — either an agent name or `user` (meaning a human verifies). ### Agent Owner If `owner` is your agent name: 1. Read the task spec and its **Verification** section. 2. Check each verification item against the artifacts and changes produced. 3. If ALL items pass: run `/openstation.verify ` to transition to `verified`, then `/openstation.done ` to complete the task. 4. If ANY item fails: set `status: rejected` and document which items failed and why (add a note in the task body or as an artifact). ### User Owner If `owner` is `user`, a human operator handles verification. Do not verify on their behalf.

15	    from artifacts_os.core.registry import Registry
16

18	_PREFIXED_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^([a-z]+)(\d+)$")
19	_ALL_DIGITS_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+$")
20	
21

23	    if registry.root is None:
24	        raise RuntimeError("Registry.root is not set; cannot perform file I/O")

32	def _meta_from_file(path: Path) -> ArtifactMeta:
33	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
34	    fm, _ = _frontmatter.parse(text)
35	    name = fm.get("name", path.stem)
36	    tags = fm.get("tags", []) or []
37	    return ArtifactMeta(
38	        id=fm.get("id", ""),
39	        kind=fm.get("kind", ""),
40	        name=name,
41	        title=name,
42	        status=fm.get("status"),

44	        created=str(fm.get("created", "")),

47	    )

50	def list_artifacts(
51	    registry: "Registry",
52	    *,
53	    kind: str | None = None,
54	    status: str | None = None,
55	    tag: str | None = None,
56	) -> list[ArtifactMeta]:
57	    """List artifacts; optionally filter by kind, status, or tag."""
58	    _require_root(registry)
59	    kinds = [registry.get(kind)] if kind else registry.all()
60	
61	    results: list[ArtifactMeta] = []
62	    for kd in kinds:
63	        subdir = _kind_dir(registry, kd)
64	        if not subdir.is_dir():
65	            continue
66	        for path in sorted(subdir.glob("*.md")):
67	            meta = _meta_from_file(path)
68	            if status is not None and meta.status != status:
69	                continue
70	            if tag is not None and tag not in meta.tags:
71	                continue
72	            results.append(meta)
73	    return results
74	
75	
76	def _find_in_dir(subdir: Path, query: str, kind_prefix: str) -> list[Path]:
77	    """Apply match strategies and return candidates (may be 0, 1, or >1)."""
78	    if not subdir.is_dir():
79	        return []
80	
81	    all_mds = list(subdir.glob("*.md"))
82	
83	    # 1. Exact stem
84	    exact = [p for p in all_mds if p.stem == query]
85	    if len(exact) == 1:
86	        return exact
87	
88	    # 2. Prefixed short/full ID (e.g. t42 → t0042)
89	    m = _PREFIXED_ID_RE.match(query)
90	    if m:
91	        letters, digits = m.group(1), m.group(2)
92	        expanded = f"{letters}{int(digits):04d}"
93	        prefixed = [
94	            p
95	            for p in all_mds
96	            if p.stem == expanded or p.stem.startswith(f"{expanded}-")
97	        ]
98	        if len(prefixed) == 1:
99	            return prefixed
100	        if prefixed:
101	            return prefixed
102	
103	    # 3. Old-style numeric (all digits)
104	    if _ALL_DIGITS_RE.match(query):
105	        padded = query.zfill(4)
106	        numeric = [
107	            p
108	            for p in all_mds
109	            if p.stem.startswith(f"{padded}-")
110	            or (kind_prefix and p.stem.startswith(f"{kind_prefix}{padded}-"))
111	        ]
112	        if len(numeric) == 1:
113	            return numeric
114	        if numeric:
115	            return numeric
116	
117	    # 4. Partial stem
118	    partial = [p for p in all_mds if query in p.stem]
119	    return partial
120	
121	
122	def _resolve_in_kind(
123	    registry: "Registry", query: str, kd: KindDef
124	) -> list[Path]:
125	    return _find_in_dir(_kind_dir(registry, kd), query, kd.prefix)
126	
127	
128	def resolve(
129	    registry: "Registry",
130	    query: str,
131	    *,
132	    kind: str | None = None,
133	) -> Path:
134	    """Resolve a query to a single Path. Raises NotFound or Ambiguous."""
135	    _require_root(registry)
136	
137	    if kind is not None:
138	        kd = registry.get(kind)
139	        matches = _resolve_in_kind(registry, query, kd)
140	        return _pick_one(matches, query)
141	
142	    # All kinds: first kind directory with an unambiguous single match wins.
143	    candidates_per_kind: list[list[Path]] = []
144	    for kd in registry.all():
145	        matches = _resolve_in_kind(registry, query, kd)
146	        if len(matches) == 1:
147	            return matches[0]
148	        if matches:
149	            candidates_per_kind.append(matches)
150	
151	    merged: list[Path] = [p for group in candidates_per_kind for p in group]
152	    return _pick_one(merged, query)
153	
154	
155	def _pick_one(matches: list[Path], query: str) -> Path:
156	    if not matches:
157	        raise NotFoundError(f"No artifact matches {query!r}")
158	    if len(matches) == 1:
159	        return matches[0]
160	    exact = [p for p in matches if p.stem == query]
161	    if len(exact) == 1:
162	        return exact[0]
163	    listing = "\n  ".join(str(p) for p in matches)
164	    raise AmbiguousError(
165	        f"Query {query!r} matches multiple artifacts:\n  {listing}"
166	    )
167	
168	
169	def search(
170	    registry: "Registry",
171	    query: str,
172	    *,
173	    kind: str | None = None,
174	) -> list[ArtifactMeta]:
175	    """Like resolve, but returns all matches as ArtifactMeta (no raises)."""
176	    _require_root(registry)
177	
178	    kinds = [registry.get(kind)] if kind else registry.all()
179	    all_matches: list[Path] = []
180	    seen: set[Path] = set()
181	    for kd in kinds:
182	        for path in _resolve_in_kind(registry, query, kd):
183	            if path not in seen:
184	                seen.add(path)
185	                all_matches.append(path)
186	
187	    return [_meta_from_file(p) for p in sorted(all_matches)]

"""Artifact CRUD: create, get, update.

Spec: s2060-artifacts-os-architecture § store.py
"""

import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import jsonschema

from artifacts_os.core import frontmatter as _frontmatter
from artifacts_os.core.errors import ValidationError
from artifacts_os.core.ids import next_prefixed_id, slugify
from artifacts_os.core.models import Artifact, ArtifactMeta, KindDef

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from artifacts_os.core.registry import Registry


_H1_RE = re.compile(r"^#\s+(.+?)\s*$", re.MULTILINE)


def _require_root(registry: "Registry") -> Path:
    if registry.root is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Registry.root is not set; cannot perform file I/O")
    return registry.root


def _kind_dir(registry: "Registry", kd: KindDef) -> Path:
    return _require_root(registry) / "openstation" / kd.dir


def _validate_schema(kd: KindDef, meta: dict) -> None:
    if not kd.schema:
        return
    try:
        jsonschema.validate(meta, kd.schema)
    except jsonschema.ValidationError as e:
        raise ValidationError(str(e)) from e


def _extract_title(body: str, fallback: str) -> str:
    match = _H1_RE.search(body)
    if match:
        return match.group(1).strip()
    return fallback


def _build_artifact(
    path: Path, meta: dict, body: str, *, read_title: bool = True
) -> Artifact:
    name = meta.get("name", path.stem)
    title = _extract_title(body, name) if read_title else name
    tags = meta.get("tags", []) or []
    return Artifact(
        id=meta.get("id", ""),
        kind=meta.get("kind", ""),
        name=name,
        title=title,
        status=meta.get("status"),
        tags=list(tags),
        created=str(meta.get("created", "")),
        path=path,
        frontmatter=dict(meta),
        body=body,
    )


def create(
    registry: "Registry",
    kind: str,
    title: str,
    *,
    body: str = "",
    fields: dict | None = None,
) -> Artifact:
    """Create a new artifact. Returns the full Artifact."""
    fields = fields or {}
    kd = registry.get(kind)
    subdir = _kind_dir(registry, kd)
    subdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    slug = slugify(title)
    if not slug:
        raise ValidationError(f"Cannot derive slug from title: {title!r}")

    if kd.numbered:
        last_err: OSError | None = None
        for _ in range(5):
            aid = next_prefixed_id(subdir, kd.prefix)
            name = f"{aid}-{slug}"
            path = subdir / f"{name}.md"
            try:
                fd = os.open(
                    path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644
                )
                break
            except FileExistsError as e:
                last_err = e
                continue
        else:
            raise last_err or FileExistsError(
                "Exhausted retries allocating numbered ID"
            )
    else:
        aid = slug
        name = slug
        path = subdir / f"{name}.md"
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)

    fm_dict: dict = {"kind": kind, "id": aid, "name": name, **fields}
    _validate_schema(kd, fm_dict)

    text = _frontmatter.dump(fm_dict, body)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(text)
    except Exception:
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise

    parsed_meta, parsed_body = _frontmatter.parse(text)
    return _build_artifact(path, parsed_meta, parsed_body)


def get(
    registry: "Registry",
    ref: str,
    *,
    kind: str | None = None,
) -> Artifact:
    """Resolve ref, read file, return Artifact (with body)."""
    from artifacts_os.core.discover import resolve

    path = resolve(registry, ref, kind=kind)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    meta, body = _frontmatter.parse(text)
    return _build_artifact(path, meta, body)


def update(
    registry: "Registry",
    ref: str,
    *,
    status: str | None = None,
    fields: dict | None = None,
) -> Artifact:
    """Merge frontmatter updates. Body preserved verbatim."""
    from artifacts_os.core.discover import resolve

    fields = fields or {}
    path = resolve(registry, ref)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    meta, body = _frontmatter.parse(text)

    kind = meta.get("kind")
    if not kind:
        raise ValidationError(f"Artifact missing 'kind': {path}")
    kd = registry.get(kind)

    if status is not None and kd.statuses and status not in kd.statuses:
        raise ValidationError(
            f"Invalid status {status!r} for kind {kind!r}. "
            f"Allowed: {kd.statuses}"
        )

    new_meta: dict = {**meta, **fields}
    if status is not None:
        new_meta["status"] = status

    _validate_schema(kd, new_meta)

    new_text = _frontmatter.dump(new_meta, body)
    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(new_text, encoding="utf-8")
    os.replace(tmp, path)

    parsed_meta, parsed_body = _frontmatter.parse(new_text)
    return _build_artifact(path, parsed_meta, parsed_body)

2	
3	Spec: s2060-artifacts-os-architecture § registry.py
4	"""

6	import json
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	from artifacts_os.core.errors import ValidationError
10	from artifacts_os.core.models import KindDef
11	
12	
13	class Registry:
14	    def __init__(
15	        self,
16	        kinds: list[KindDef],
17	        root: Path | None = None,
18	    ) -> None:
19	        self._root = Path(root).resolve() if root is not None else None
20	        self._kinds: dict[str, KindDef] = {kd.name: kd for kd in kinds}
21	        if self._root is not None:
22	            for kd in self._load_vault_kinds(self._root):
23	                self._kinds[kd.name] = kd
24	
25	    @property
26	    def root(self) -> Path | None:
27	        return self._root
28	
29	    def get(self, kind: str) -> KindDef:
30	        if kind not in self._kinds:
31	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown kind: {kind!r}")
32	        return self._kinds[kind]
33	
34	    def all(self) -> list[KindDef]:
35	        return list(self._kinds.values())
36	
37	    def for_dir(self, dir_name: str) -> KindDef | None:
38	        for kd in self._kinds.values():
39	            if kd.dir == dir_name:
40	                return kd
41	        return None
42	
43	    @staticmethod
44	    def _load_vault_kinds(root: Path) -> list[KindDef]:
45	        types_dir = root / "openstation" / "types"
46	        if not types_dir.is_dir():
47	            return []
48	        out: list[KindDef] = []
49	        for path in sorted(types_dir.glob("*.json")):
50	            with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
51	                schema = json.load(f)
52	            if not isinstance(schema, dict):
53	                raise ValidationError(
54	                    f"Vault kind schema must be an object: {path}"
55	                )
56	            kind_dir = schema.get("x-dir")
57	            if not kind_dir:
58	                raise ValidationError(
59	                    f"Vault kind schema missing required 'x-dir': {path}"
60	                )
61	            statuses = (
62	                schema.get("properties", {})
63	                .get("status", {})
64	                .get("enum", [])
65	            )
66	            meta: dict = {}
67	            if "x-columns" in schema:
68	                meta["columns"] = schema["x-columns"]
69	            if "x-status-colors" in schema:
70	                meta["status_colors"] = schema["x-status-colors"]
71	            out.append(
72	                KindDef(
73	                    name=path.stem,
74	                    dir=kind_dir,
75	                    prefix=schema.get("x-prefix", ""),
76	                    numbered=bool(schema.get("x-numbered", True)),
77	                    statuses=list(statuses),
78	                    schema=schema,
79	                    meta=meta,
80	                )
81	            )
82	        return out
83

        (root / ".openstation").mkdir(parents=True)
        (root / "openstation").mkdir()
        ks = kinds if kinds is not None else _default_kinds()
        for kd in ks:
            (root / "openstation" / kd.dir).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        registry = Registry(ks, root=root)
        return root, registry

    return _make

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from artifacts_os import KindDef, Registry
from artifacts_os.core.errors import ValidationError


def _write_schema(root: Path, name: str, schema: dict) -> None:
    types = root / "openstation" / "types"
    types.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (types / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(schema), encoding="utf-8")


def test_no_root_no_scan() -> None:
    kinds = [KindDef(name="task", dir="tasks", prefix="t", numbered=True)]
    r = Registry(kinds)
    assert r.root is None
    assert r.get("task").name == "task"
    assert len(r.all()) == 1


def test_unknown_kind_raises() -> None:
    r = Registry([])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        r.get("nope")


def test_for_dir_lookup() -> None:
    kinds = [
        KindDef(name="task", dir="tasks", prefix="t", numbered=True),
        KindDef(name="agent", dir="agents", prefix="", numbered=False),
    ]
    r = Registry(kinds)
    assert r.for_dir("tasks").name == "task"
    assert r.for_dir("nonexistent") is None


def test_vault_types_scan(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = tmp_path / "vault"
    (root / ".openstation").mkdir(parents=True)
    _write_schema(
        root,
        "changelog",
        {
            "x-prefix": "c",
            "x-numbered": True,
            "x-dir": "changelogs",
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "status": {"enum": ["draft", "published"]},
            },
        },
    )
    r = Registry([], root=root)
    kd = r.get("changelog")
    assert kd.dir == "changelogs"
    assert kd.prefix == "c"
    assert kd.numbered is True
    assert kd.statuses == ["draft", "published"]


def test_vault_override_caller_kind(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = tmp_path / "vault"
    (root / ".openstation").mkdir(parents=True)
    _write_schema(
        root,
        "task",
        {"x-prefix": "xx", "x-numbered": True, "x-dir": "custom"},
    )
    caller_kinds = [KindDef(name="task", dir="tasks", prefix="t", numbered=True)]
    r = Registry(caller_kinds, root=root)
    kd = r.get("task")
    assert kd.prefix == "xx"
    assert kd.dir == "custom"


def test_missing_x_dir_raises(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = tmp_path / "vault"
    (root / ".openstation").mkdir(parents=True)
    _write_schema(root, "broken", {"x-prefix": "b"})
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Registry([], root=root)


def test_no_types_dir_is_noop(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = tmp_path / "vault"
    (root / ".openstation").mkdir(parents=True)
    r = Registry(
        [KindDef(name="task", dir="tasks", prefix="t", numbered=True)],
        root=root,
    )
    assert [kd.name for kd in r.all()] == ["task"]

import pytest

from artifacts_os import KindDef, Registry, create, get, update
from artifacts_os.core.errors import ValidationError


def test_create_numbered(make_vault) -> None:
    root, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(registry, "task", "Fix the bug")
    assert a.id == "t0001"
    assert a.name == "t0001-fix-the-bug"
    assert a.path.name == "t0001-fix-the-bug.md"
    assert a.path.parent == root / "openstation" / "tasks"


def test_create_increments(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    create(registry, "task", "First")
    a = create(registry, "task", "Second")
    assert a.id == "t0002"


def test_create_non_numbered_agent(make_vault) -> None:
    root, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(registry, "agent", "researcher")
    assert a.id == "researcher"
    assert a.name == "researcher"
    assert a.path.name == "researcher.md"


def test_create_non_numbered_collision(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    create(registry, "agent", "researcher")
    with pytest.raises(FileExistsError):
        create(registry, "agent", "researcher")


def test_create_empty_title_raises(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        create(registry, "task", "!!!")


def test_create_schema_validation_fails(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = tmp_path / "vault"
    (root / ".openstation").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "openstation" / "tasks").mkdir(parents=True)
    kinds = [
        KindDef(
            name="task",
            dir="tasks",
            prefix="t",
            numbered=True,
            schema={
                "type": "object",
                "required": ["priority"],
                "properties": {"priority": {"type": "string"}},
                "additionalProperties": True,
            },
        )
    ]
    registry = Registry(kinds, root=root)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        create(registry, "task", "No priority field")


def test_get_reads_body_and_title(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(
        registry,
        "task",
        "Title",
        body="# Real H1 Title\n\nBody content.",
    )
    fetched = get(registry, a.id)
    assert fetched.title == "Real H1 Title"
    assert "Body content." in fetched.body


def test_get_no_h1_falls_back_to_name(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(registry, "task", "Fix it", body="Plain body with no heading.")
    fetched = get(registry, a.id)
    assert fetched.title == a.name


def test_update_status(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(registry, "task", "Do something")
    updated = update(registry, a.id, status="ready")
    assert updated.status == "ready"


def test_update_invalid_status(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(registry, "task", "Do something")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        update(registry, a.id, status="bogus")


def test_update_preserves_body(make_vault) -> None:
    _, registry = make_vault()
    body = "# Heading\n\nKeep me verbatim.\n"
    a = create(registry, "task", "T", body=body)
    updated = update(registry, a.id, status="ready")
    text = updated.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "Keep me verbatim." in text

    _, registry = make_vault()
    a = create(registry, "task", "T", fields={"owner": "alice"})
    updated = update(registry, a.id, fields={"priority": "high"})
    assert updated.frontmatter["owner"] == "alice"
    assert updated.frontmatter["priority"] == "high"

"""Integration tests for cli validate command."""

import json

import pytest

from artifacts_os.cli import main


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test cases
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_all_valid_vault_returns_0(vault, write_artifact):
    """Vault with all valid artifacts exits 0."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-fix-bug.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-fix-bug",
                    "title": "Fix bug", "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "ready"})
    # No SystemExit means exit code 0
    main(["validate"])


def test_vault_with_error_returns_2(vault, write_artifact, capsys):
    """Vault with one bad artifact (error) exits 2 and JSON output contains name."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-broken.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-broken",
                    "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "ready"})
    # missing title → error

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        main(["validate", "-j"])
    assert exc.value.code == 2

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    data = json.loads(out)
    assert any(r["name"] == "t0001-broken" for r in data)


def test_vault_with_only_warnings_returns_0(vault, write_artifact, capsys):
    """Vault with only warnings exits 0; warnings appear in JSON output."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-test.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-test",
                    "title": "Test", "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "ready",
                    "weirdkey": "value"})  # unknown field → warning

    main(["validate", "-j"])  # exits 0

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    data = json.loads(out)
    # weirdkey warning should appear in JSON output
    assert len(data) >= 1
    warnings = [i for i in data[0]["issues"] if i["severity"] == "warning"]
    assert any(i["field"] == "weirdkey" for i in warnings)


def test_json_output(vault, write_artifact, capsys):
    """--json output is valid JSON and each issue has a severity key."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-broken.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-broken",
                    "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "ready"})
    # missing title → error

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        main(["validate", "-j"])
    assert exc.value.code == 2

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    data = json.loads(out)
    assert isinstance(data, list)
    assert len(data) >= 1
    issues = data[0]["issues"]
    assert all("severity" in i for i in issues)


def test_fix_corrects_status(vault, write_artifact):
    """--fix corrects bad status; re-validate returns 0."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-broken.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-broken",
                    "title": "Test", "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "wip"})
    # bad status → error, fixable

    # First validate fails
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        main(["validate"])
    assert exc.value.code == 2

    # Fix it
    main(["validate", "--fix"])

    # Now re-validate should pass
    main(["validate"])


def test_fix_does_not_touch_warnings(vault, write_artifact, capsys):
    """--fix does not remove unknown fields (warnings)."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-test.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-test",
                    "title": "Test", "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "ready",
                    "weirdkey": "value"})

    main(["validate", "--fix"])  # fix runs; exits 0 (only warnings)

    # weirdkey should still be there
    path = vault / "openstation" / "tasks" / "t0001-test.md"
    content = path.read_text()
    assert "weirdkey" in content


def test_dry_run_does_not_write(vault, write_artifact):
    """--dry-run produces no writes even when fixes are available."""
    path = write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-broken.md",
                          {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-broken",
                           "title": "Test", "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "wip"})
    original_content = path.read_text()

    # dry-run still reports errors (exits 2), but must not write
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        main(["validate", "--dry-run"])
    assert exc.value.code == 2

    # File must be unchanged
    assert path.read_text() == original_content


def test_ref_not_found_exits_3(vault):
    """<ref> not found raises NotFoundError → exit 3."""
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        main(["validate", "nonexistent-artifact"])
    assert exc.value.code == 3


def test_kind_filter(vault, write_artifact, capsys):
    """--kind filter validates only named kind."""
    write_artifact(vault, "tasks", "t0001-good-task.md",
                   {"kind": "task", "id": "t0001", "name": "t0001-good-task",
                    "title": "Good", "created": "2026-01-01", "status": "ready"})
    write_artifact(vault, "agents", "bad-agent.md",
                   {"kind": "agent", "id": "bad-agent", "name": "bad-agent",
                    "created": "2026-01-01"})
    # agent missing title → error, but we only validate "task" kind

    # Validate only tasks — should exit 0 (task is valid)
    main(["validate", "--kind", "task"])

1	# artifacts-os Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-04-20  
4	**Status:** approved  
5	**Author:** Leon Prouger
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Overview
10	
11	Extract OpenStation's artifact storage layer into a standalone Python
12	package called `artifacts-os`. The package owns kind definitions,
13	frontmatter parsing, ID generation, file creation, discovery, and
14	resolution. OpenStation depends on it as a local editable install and
15	extends it with display and operational metadata.
16	
17	**Goals:**
18	- **Reuse** — other projects can use the same artifact primitives
19	- **Separation of concerns** — storage layer is independently testable
20	- **Extensibility** — vault owners add custom kinds by dropping a JSON
21	  schema file; no code required
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Repository Layout
26	
27	`artifacts-os` lives as a sibling directory to `open-station`:
28	
29	```
30	~/workspace/
31	  open-station/      # existing repo
32	  artifacts-os/      # new package
33	```
34	
35	OpenStation declares the dependency in `pyproject.toml`:
36	
37	```toml
38	dependencies = [
39	    "artifacts-os",
40	    ...
41	]
42	```
43	
44	Local development uses an editable install:
45	
46	```bash
47	pip install -e ../artifacts-os
48	```
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Package Layout
53	
54	```
55	artifacts-os/
56	  src/
57	    artifacts_os/
58	      __init__.py          # public API re-exports
59	      models.py            # KindDef, ArtifactMeta, Artifact
60	      errors.py            # ArtifactError, NotFoundError, AmbiguousError, ValidationError
61	      frontmatter.py       # parse/dump via python-frontmatter
62	      registry.py          # Registry class — merges caller kinds + vault types/
63	      ids.py               # next_prefixed_id, slugify, validate_slug
64	      store.py             # create, get, update (atomic writes)
65	      discover.py          # list_artifacts, resolve, search
66	      vault.py             # find_vault_root (marker-based)
67	  pyproject.toml
68	  tests/
69	```
70	
71	`artifacts-os` ships **no built-in kind schemas**. It is kind-agnostic.
72	Callers (e.g. OpenStation) define their own kinds as `KindDef` objects
73	in code and pass them to the `Registry`. Vault owners extend with
74	custom JSON schemas dropped in `openstation/types/`.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Vault Structure
79	
80	`artifacts-os` is opinionated about layout. The vault marker is
81	`.openstation/` at the project root; `find_vault_root` walks up the
82	directory tree until it finds it.
83	
84	```
85	<project>/
86	  .openstation/          # vault marker
87	  openstation/
88	    tasks/               # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: t)
89	    specs/               # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: s)
90	    research/            # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: r)
91	    notes/               # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: n)
92	    alerts/              # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: a)
93	    agents/              # slug.md       (no prefix, no number)
94	    types/               # user-defined kind schemas (*.json)
95	```
96	
97	---
98	
99	## Kind Definitions
100	
101	### Code-defined (primary)
102	
103	Callers define kinds as `KindDef` objects directly in Python and pass
104	them to `Registry`. This is how OpenStation registers its built-in
105	kinds (task, spec, research, note, alert, agent) — no JSON files
106	required.
107	
108	```python
109	from artifacts_os import Registry, KindDef
110	
111	registry = Registry([
112	    KindDef(name="task",     dir="tasks",    prefix="t", numbered=True,
113	            statuses=["backlog", "ready", "in-progress", "review",
114	                      "verified", "done", "failed", "rejected"]),
115	    KindDef(name="agent",    dir="agents",   prefix="",  numbered=False,
116	            statuses=[]),
117	    KindDef(name="research", dir="research", prefix="r", numbered=True,
118	            statuses=[]),
119	    # ...
120	], root=root)  # root triggers vault types/ scan on top
121	```
122	
123	### Vault-defined (extensibility)
124	
125	Vault owners add custom kinds by dropping a JSON Schema file in
126	`openstation/types/`. The `Registry` merges these on top of the
127	caller-provided kinds when `root` is given. Vault schemas can also
128	override a caller-provided kind by using the same `name`.
129	
130	JSON schemas use `x-` extension fields to control storage behaviour:
131	
132	| Extension field | Type | Meaning |
133	|---|---|---|
134	| `x-prefix` | string | ID prefix (`"c"` → `c0001`); empty = no prefix |
135	| `x-numbered` | bool | `true` = `NNNN-slug.md`; `false` = `slug.md` |
136	| `x-dir` | string | Subdirectory under `openstation/` |
137	
138	**Statuses** are extracted from `properties.status.enum` at load time.
139	Kinds with no `status` property have `statuses: []`.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## Extensibility — Custom Kinds
144	
145	Vault owners add a kind by dropping a JSON schema file in
146	`openstation/types/`. No Python required.
147	
148	**Example — `openstation/types/changelog.json`:**
149	
150	```json
151	{
152	  "x-prefix": "c",
153	  "x-numbered": true,
154	  "x-dir": "changelogs",
155	  "type": "object",
156	  "required": ["kind", "name"],
157	  "properties": {
158	    "kind":    { "const": "changelog" },
159	    "name":    { "type": "string" },
160	    "version": { "type": "string" }
161	  },
162	  "additionalProperties": true
163	}
164	```
165	
166	`Registry` merges vault-defined kinds on top of the caller-provided
167	kinds. A vault schema with the same name as a caller-provided kind
168	overrides it entirely — enabling full customisation without forking.
169	
170	---
171	
172	## Data Models
173	
174	```python
175	@dataclass
176	class KindDef:
177	    name: str            # "task"
178	    dir: str             # "tasks"
179	    prefix: str          # "t" (empty string for agents)
180	    numbered: bool       # True = NNNN-slug, False = slug-only
181	    statuses: list[str]  # [] if kind has no status concept
182	    schema: dict         # full JSON Schema dict
183	    meta: dict           # caller-defined extras; library never reads this
184	
185	@dataclass
186	class ArtifactMeta:
187	    """Lightweight metadata from frontmatter only. Used for listing."""
188	    id: str              # "t0042" or "researcher" (agents)
189	    kind: str            # "task"
190	    name: str            # slug: "fix-the-bug"
191	    title: str           # human-readable title
192	    status: str | None
193	    tags: list[str]
194	    created: str         # ISO date string
195	    path: Path
196	    frontmatter: dict    # all raw frontmatter fields
197	
198	@dataclass
199	class Artifact(ArtifactMeta):
200	    """Full artifact including body. Used for get/create/update."""
201	    body: str
202	```
203	
204	The `meta: dict` slot on `KindDef` is where OpenStation attaches
205	`default_columns`, `renderer`, `filterable_by`, and custom `discover`.
206	The library never reads `meta`.
207	
208	---
209	
210	## Error Hierarchy
211	
212	Exceptions replace the current `(path, error_msg, exit_code)` tuple
213	returns throughout OpenStation. The CLI layer catches them and maps to
214	exit codes.
215	
216	```python
217	class ArtifactError(Exception):    # base; exit code 1
218	class NotFoundError(ArtifactError): pass   # exit code 3
219	class AmbiguousError(ArtifactError): pass  # exit code 4
220	class ValidationError(ArtifactError): pass # exit code 2
221	```
222	
223	---
224	
225	## Public API
226	
227	```python
228	from artifacts_os import (
229	    # Vault
230	    find_vault_root,     # (start: Path) -> Path
231	
232	    # Registry
233	    Registry,            # Registry(kinds: list[KindDef], root: Path | None = None)
234	                         #   .get(kind: str) -> KindDef
235	                         #   .all() -> list[KindDef]
236	
237	    # CRUD
238	    create,              # (registry, kind, title, *, body="", fields={}) -> Artifact
239	    get,                 # (registry, ref, *, kind=None) -> Artifact
240	    list_artifacts,      # (registry, *, kind=None, status=None, tag=None) -> list[ArtifactMeta]
241	    update,              # (registry, ref, *, status=None, fields={}) -> Artifact
242	    search,              # (registry, query, *, kind=None) -> list[ArtifactMeta]
243	    resolve,             # (registry, query, *, kind=None) -> Path
244	
245	    # Models
246	    Artifact, ArtifactMeta, KindDef,
247	
248	    # Errors
249	    ArtifactError, NotFoundError, AmbiguousError, ValidationError,
250	)
251	```
252	
253	`Registry(kinds, root=root)` — builds from caller-provided `KindDef`
254	objects, then scans `root/openstation/types/*.json` and merges any
255	vault-defined kinds on top. Pass `root=None` to skip vault scanning.
256	
257	`resolve` accepts prefixed IDs (`t42`, `t0042`), full stems
258	(`0042-fix-the-bug`), agent names (`researcher`), and partial slug
259	matches. Returns `Path` on success; raises `NotFoundError` or
260	`AmbiguousError` on failure.
261	
262	---
263	
264	## OpenStation Integration
265	
266	### registry.py
267	
268	```python
269	from dataclasses import replace
270	from artifacts_os import load_registry
271	
272	_DISPLAY: dict[str, dict] = {
273	    "task": {
274	        "default_columns": ["id", "status", "assignee", "owner", "name"],
275	        "renderer": "task",
276	        "filterable_by": ["status", "assignee", "type", "owner"],
277	        "discover": discover_tasks,
278	    },
279	    "research": {
280	        "default_columns": ["id", "name", "summary"],
281	        "renderer": "artifact",
282	        "filterable_by": ["type"],
283	    },
284	    # ... other kinds
285	}
286	
287	def build_registry(root: Path) -> dict:
288	    base = load_registry(root)
289	    return {
290	        name: replace(kd, meta=_DISPLAY.get(name, {}))
291	        for name, kd in base.items()
292	    }
293	```
294	
295	### artifacts.py / tasks.py
296	
297	Discovery, resolution, and creation logic delegates to `artifacts_os`:
298	
299	```python
300	from artifacts_os import list_artifacts, resolve, create
301	
302	# Before (OpenStation)
303	artifacts = discover_artifacts(root, kind=kind)
304	path, err, code = resolve_artifact(root, query)
305	
306	# After
307	artifacts = list_artifacts(root, kind=kind)
308	path = resolve(root, query, kind=kind)   # raises on failure
309	```

311	### CLI error handling

314	try:
315	    path = resolve(root, query)
316	except NotFoundError as e:
317	    core.err(str(e))
318	    return core.EXIT_NOT_FOUND
319	except AmbiguousError as e:
320	    core.err(str(e))
321	    return core.EXIT_AMBIGUOUS
322	```
323	
324	---
325	
326	## Dependencies
327	
328	`artifacts-os` dependencies are minimal:
329	
330	```toml
331	dependencies = [
332	    "python-frontmatter>=1.1",
333	    "jsonschema>=4.23",
334	]
335	```
336	
337	`python-frontmatter` replaces OpenStation's hand-rolled YAML parser.
338	`jsonschema` validates frontmatter against kind schemas on create/update.
339	
340	Git auto-commit (from the PoC) is **not included** — OpenStation manages
341	its own git operations.

347	### Moves to `artifacts-os`

350	|---|---|
351	| `core.parse_frontmatter`, `extract_body`, `parse_multiline_value` | `artifacts_os.frontmatter` |
352	| `core.next_prefixed_id` | `artifacts_os.ids` |

354	| `artifacts.create_artifact_file` | `artifacts_os.store` |
355	| `artifacts.discover_artifacts` | `artifacts_os.discover` |
356	| `artifacts.resolve_artifact`, `resolve_artifact_for_kind` | `artifacts_os.discover` |
357	| `registry.resolve_any` | `artifacts_os.discover` |

362	|---|---|

# artifacts-os Design

**Date:** 2026-04-20  
**Status:** approved  
**Author:** Leon Prouger

---

## Overview

Extract OpenStation's artifact storage layer into a standalone Python
package called `artifacts-os`. The package owns kind definitions,
frontmatter parsing, ID generation, file creation, discovery, and
resolution. OpenStation depends on it as a local editable install and
extends it with display and operational metadata.

**Goals:**
- **Reuse** — other projects can use the same artifact primitives
- **Separation of concerns** — storage layer is independently testable
- **Extensibility** — vault owners add custom kinds by dropping a JSON
  schema file; no code required

---

## Repository Layout

`artifacts-os` lives as a sibling directory to `open-station`:

```
~/workspace/
  open-station/      # existing repo
  artifacts-os/      # new package
```

OpenStation declares the dependency in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
dependencies = [
    "artifacts-os",
    ...
]
```

Local development uses an editable install:

```bash
pip install -e ../artifacts-os
```

---

## Package Layout

```
artifacts-os/
  src/
    artifacts_os/
      __init__.py          # public API re-exports
      models.py            # KindDef, ArtifactMeta, Artifact
      errors.py            # ArtifactError, NotFoundError, AmbiguousError, ValidationError
      frontmatter.py       # parse/dump via python-frontmatter
      registry.py          # Registry class — merges caller kinds + vault types/
      ids.py               # next_prefixed_id, slugify, validate_slug
      store.py             # create, get, update (atomic writes)
      discover.py          # list_artifacts, resolve, search
      vault.py             # find_vault_root (marker-based)
  pyproject.toml
  tests/
```

`artifacts-os` ships **no built-in kind schemas**. It is kind-agnostic.
Callers (e.g. OpenStation) define their own kinds as `KindDef` objects
in code and pass them to the `Registry`. Vault owners extend with
custom JSON schemas dropped in `openstation/types/`.

---

## Vault Structure

`artifacts-os` is opinionated about layout. The vault marker is
`.openstation/` at the project root; `find_vault_root` walks up the
directory tree until it finds it.

```
<project>/
  .openstation/          # vault marker
  openstation/
    tasks/               # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: t)
    specs/               # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: s)
    research/            # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: r)
    notes/               # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: n)
    alerts/              # NNNN-slug.md  (prefix: a)
    agents/              # slug.md       (no prefix, no number)
    types/               # user-defined kind schemas (*.json)
```

---

## Kind Definitions

### Code-defined (primary)

Callers define kinds as `KindDef` objects directly in Python and pass
them to `Registry`. This is how OpenStation registers its built-in
kinds (task, spec, research, note, alert, agent) — no JSON files
required.

```python
from artifacts_os import Registry, KindDef

registry = Registry([
    KindDef(name="task",     dir="tasks",    prefix="t", numbered=True,
            statuses=["backlog", "ready", "in-progress", "review",
                      "verified", "done", "failed", "rejected"]),
    KindDef(name="agent",    dir="agents",   prefix="",  numbered=False,
            statuses=[]),
    KindDef(name="research", dir="research", prefix="r", numbered=True,
            statuses=[]),
    # ...
], root=root)  # root triggers vault types/ scan on top
```

### Vault-defined (extensibility)

Vault owners add custom kinds by dropping a JSON Schema file in
`openstation/types/`. The `Registry` merges these on top of the
caller-provided kinds when `root` is given. Vault schemas can also
override a caller-provided kind by using the same `name`.

JSON schemas use `x-` extension fields to control storage behaviour:

| Extension field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `x-prefix` | string | ID prefix (`"c"` → `c0001`); empty = no prefix |
| `x-numbered` | bool | `true` = `NNNN-slug.md`; `false` = `slug.md` |
| `x-dir` | string | Subdirectory under `openstation/` |

**Statuses** are extracted from `properties.status.enum` at load time.
Kinds with no `status` property have `statuses: []`.

---

## Extensibility — Custom Kinds

Vault owners add a kind by dropping a JSON schema file in
`openstation/types/`. No Python required.

**Example — `openstation/types/changelog.json`:**

```json
{
  "x-prefix": "c",
  "x-numbered": true,
  "x-dir": "changelogs",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["kind", "name"],
  "properties": {
    "kind":    { "const": "changelog" },
    "name":    { "type": "string" },
    "version": { "type": "string" }
  },
  "additionalProperties": true
}
```

`Registry` merges vault-defined kinds on top of the caller-provided
kinds. A vault schema with the same name as a caller-provided kind
overrides it entirely — enabling full customisation without forking.

---

## Data Models

```python
@dataclass
class KindDef:
    name: str            # "task"
    dir: str             # "tasks"
    prefix: str          # "t" (empty string for agents)
    numbered: bool       # True = NNNN-slug, False = slug-only
    statuses: list[str]  # [] if kind has no status concept
    schema: dict         # full JSON Schema dict
    meta: dict           # caller-defined extras; library never reads this

@dataclass
class ArtifactMeta:
    """Lightweight metadata from frontmatter only. Used for listing."""
    id: str              # "t0042" or "researcher" (agents)
    kind: str            # "task"
    name: str            # slug: "fix-the-bug"
    title: str           # human-readable title
    status: str | None
    tags: list[str]
    created: str         # ISO date string
    path: Path
    frontmatter: dict    # all raw frontmatter fields

@dataclass
class Artifact(ArtifactMeta):
    """Full artifact including body. Used for get/create/update."""
    body: str
```

The `meta: dict` slot on `KindDef` is where OpenStation attaches
`default_columns`, `renderer`, `filterable_by`, and custom `discover`.
The library never reads `meta`.

---

## Error Hierarchy

Exceptions replace the current `(path, error_msg, exit_code)` tuple
returns throughout OpenStation. The CLI layer catches them and maps to
exit codes.

```python
class ArtifactError(Exception):    # base; exit code 1
class NotFoundError(ArtifactError): pass   # exit code 3
class AmbiguousError(ArtifactError): pass  # exit code 4
class ValidationError(ArtifactError): pass # exit code 2
```

---

## Public API

```python
from artifacts_os import (
    # Vault
    find_vault_root,     # (start: Path) -> Path

    # Registry
    Registry,            # Registry(kinds: list[KindDef], root: Path | None = None)
                         #   .get(kind: str) -> KindDef
                         #   .all() -> list[KindDef]

    # CRUD
    create,              # (registry, kind, title, *, body="", fields={}) -> Artifact
    get,                 # (registry, ref, *, kind=None) -> Artifact
    list_artifacts,      # (registry, *, kind=None, status=None, tag=None) -> list[ArtifactMeta]
    update,              # (registry, ref, *, status=None, fields={}) -> Artifact
    search,              # (registry, query, *, kind=None) -> list[ArtifactMeta]
    resolve,             # (registry, query, *, kind=None) -> Path

    # Models
    Artifact, ArtifactMeta, KindDef,

    # Errors
    ArtifactError, NotFoundError, AmbiguousError, ValidationError,
)
```

`Registry(kinds, root=root)` — builds from caller-provided `KindDef`
objects, then scans `root/openstation/types/*.json` and merges any
vault-defined kinds on top. Pass `root=None` to skip vault scanning.

`resolve` accepts prefixed IDs (`t42`, `t0042`), full stems
(`0042-fix-the-bug`), agent names (`researcher`), and partial slug
matches. Returns `Path` on success; raises `NotFoundError` or
`AmbiguousError` on failure.

---

## OpenStation Integration

### registry.py

```python
from dataclasses import replace
from artifacts_os import load_registry

_DISPLAY: dict[str, dict] = {
    "task": {
        "default_columns": ["id", "status", "assignee", "owner", "name"],
        "renderer": "task",
        "filterable_by": ["status", "assignee", "type", "owner"],
        "discover": discover_tasks,
    },
    "research": {
        "default_columns": ["id", "name", "summary"],
        "renderer": "artifact",
        "filterable_by": ["type"],
    },
    # ... other kinds
}

def build_registry(root: Path) -> dict:
    base = load_registry(root)
    return {
        name: replace(kd, meta=_DISPLAY.get(name, {}))
        for name, kd in base.items()
    }
```

### artifacts.py / tasks.py

Discovery, resolution, and creation logic delegates to `artifacts_os`:

```python
from artifacts_os import list_artifacts, resolve, create

# Before (OpenStation)
artifacts = discover_artifacts(root, kind=kind)
path, err, code = resolve_artifact(root, query)

# After
artifacts = list_artifacts(root, kind=kind)
path = resolve(root, query, kind=kind)   # raises on failure
```

### CLI error handling

```python
try:
    path = resolve(root, query)
except NotFoundError as e:
    core.err(str(e))
    return core.EXIT_NOT_FOUND
except AmbiguousError as e:
    core.err(str(e))
    return core.EXIT_AMBIGUOUS
```

---

## Dependencies

`artifacts-os` dependencies are minimal:

```toml
dependencies = [
    "python-frontmatter>=1.1",
    "jsonschema>=4.23",
]
```

`python-frontmatter` replaces OpenStation's hand-rolled YAML parser.
`jsonschema` validates frontmatter against kind schemas on create/update.

Git auto-commit (from the PoC) is **not included** — OpenStation manages
its own git operations.

---

## What Moves vs What Stays

### Moves to `artifacts-os`

| Current location | Destination |
|---|---|
| `core.parse_frontmatter`, `extract_body`, `parse_multiline_value` | `artifacts_os.frontmatter` |
| `core.next_prefixed_id` | `artifacts_os.ids` |
| `registry.ArtifactKind` | `artifacts_os.models.KindDef` |
| `artifacts.create_artifact_file` | `artifacts_os.store` |
| `artifacts.discover_artifacts` | `artifacts_os.discover` |
| `artifacts.resolve_artifact`, `resolve_artifact_for_kind` | `artifacts_os.discover` |
| `registry.resolve_any` | `artifacts_os.discover` |

### Stays in OpenStation

| Module | Reason |
|---|---|
| `registry.py` | OpenStation-specific `REGISTRY` + display metadata |
| `cli.py` | CLI parsing, argument handling, exit codes |
| `ui.py` | Rich rendering, table formatters, status colouring |
| `tasks.py` | Lifecycle transitions, task-specific discovery |
| `alerts.py` | Alert-specific discovery and scheduling logic |
| `sessions.py`, `hooks.py`, `run.py` | Agent execution, no artifact storage concern |
| `core.py` (exit codes, lifecycle) | OpenStation domain constants |

1	---
2	kind: spec
3	name: storage-query-layer
4	---
5	
6	# Storage & Query Layer
7	
8	Authoritative reference for how tasks, artifacts, and agents are
9	stored on the filesystem and how they are discovered.
10	
11	For lifecycle rules (status transitions, ownership, verification)
12	see `docs/lifecycle.md`. For task field schema and naming see
13	`docs/task.spec.md`.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Part I — Storage Layer
18	
19	### 1. Canonical Storage Model
20	
21	All persistent data lives under `openstation/`, which is the single
22	source of truth. Each artifact type has a dedicated subdirectory:
23	
24	```
25	openstation/
26	├── tasks/       — Task files (one per task, never moved)
27	├── agents/      — Agent spec files (canonical location)
28	├── notes/       — Planning notes (roadmap, release plans)
29	├── research/    — Research outputs (from researcher agent)
30	├── specs/       — Specifications and designs
31	└── logs/        — Run logs
32	```
33	
34	**Immutability rule:** Once a file is created in `openstation/`, it
35	stays at that path permanently. Nothing in `openstation/` is ever
36	moved or renamed — only its contents are updated in place.
37	
38	All artifact types are single markdown files with YAML
39	frontmatter, stored directly in their category directory:
40	
41	```
42	openstation/tasks/0010-add-login-page.md
43	openstation/agents/researcher.md
44	openstation/research/obsidian-plugin-api.md
45	openstation/specs/storage-query-layer.md
46	```
47	
48	### 1a. Artifact Naming Conventions
49	
50	Each kind uses one of two filename patterns. See `docs/artifacts.md`
51	§ "Artifact Naming" for the canonical reference, examples, and the
52	"existing artifacts are not renamed" rule. Summary:
53	
54	| Kind       | Pattern            | Example                              |
55	|------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
56	| Task       | `NNNN-kebab-slug`  | `0042-add-login-page`                |
57	| Alert      | `NNNN-kebab-slug`  | `0001-daily-standup`                 |
58	| Research   | `NNNN-kebab-slug`  | `0003-login-page-ux-research`        |
59	| Spec       | `NNNN-kebab-slug`  | `0007-storage-query-layer`           |
60	| Note       | `NNNN-kebab-slug`  | `0002-release-plan`                  |
61	| Agent      | `kebab-slug`       | `researcher`                         |
62	
63	#### Auto-assigned NNNN (All kinds except Agents)
64	
65	All artifact kinds except agents receive IDs via
66	`openstation create --kind <kind>`, which scans the kind's
67	directory for the highest `NNNN-` prefix and assigns `max + 1`.
68	IDs are:
69	
70	- 4-digit zero-padded integer (`0001`, `0042`, `0100`)
71	- Per-kind counter space (each directory independent)
72	- Assigned atomically (`O_CREAT | O_EXCL`) — never pick IDs manually
73	
74	See `docs/task.spec.md` § Naming for the full task ID spec.
75	See `docs/alerts.md` for the alert schema.
76	
77	Provenance (which task produced an artifact) is tracked via the
78	`task` frontmatter field, not the filename. Existing artifacts
79	that predate this convention are not renamed.
80	
81	#### No-prefix (Agents)
82	
83	Agents use descriptive kebab-case names with no numeric prefix.
84	The filename is the stable CLI identifier used in
85	`openstation run <name>` and must not change once set.
86	
87	### 2. Discovery Symlinks
88	
89	Open Station uses a single kind of symlink: **discovery
90	symlinks** for agent resolution. No other symlinks exist in the
91	system.
92	
93	#### 2a. Agent Discovery Symlinks
94	
95	Symlinks in `agents/` that point to canonical specs in
96	`openstation/agents/`. They make agents available via
97	`claude --agent <name>`:
98	
99	```
100	agents/researcher.md → ../../openstation/agents/researcher.md
101	```
102	
103	Discovery symlinks are created by:
104	
105	- `openstation init` — for bundled example agents at install time.
106	- `/openstation.done` — for agents produced by tasks, after
107	  verification passes (agent promotion).
108	
109	Agents must NOT create discovery symlinks during task execution.
110	
111	### 3. Frontmatter Associations
112	
113	All relationships between tasks, sub-tasks, and artifacts are
114	encoded in YAML frontmatter fields using **Obsidian wikilinks**
115	(`[[name]]`). Wikilinks make references clickable in Obsidian's
116	properties panel and graph view. Quote them for valid YAML.
117	
118	There are no symlinks for these associations.
119	
120	#### 3a. Parent → Children (subtasks)
121	
122	A parent task lists its sub-tasks in a `subtasks` frontmatter
123	field:
124	
125	```yaml
126	subtasks:
127	  - "[[0046-spec-storage-query-layer]]"
128	  - "[[0047-implement-storage-replacement]]"
129	```
130	
131	#### 3b. Child → Parent
132	
133	Each sub-task declares its parent via the `parent` field:
134	
135	```yaml
136	parent: "[[0045-replace-storage-obsidian-cli]]"
137	```
138	
139	#### 3c. Task → Artifacts
140	
141	Tasks list the artifacts they produced in the `artifacts`
142	frontmatter field:
143	
144	```yaml
145	artifacts:
146	  - "[[openstation/agents/project-manager]]"
147	  - "[[openstation/research/obsidian-plugin-api]]"
148	```
149	
150	#### 3d. Artifact Provenance
151	
152	Artifacts declare which agent generated them and which task they
153	belong to:
154	
155	```yaml
156	agent: researcher
157	task: "[[0044-storage-layer-replacement]]"
158	```
159	
160	Use `agent: manual` and omit `task` for manually created
161	artifacts. These fields are optional — not all artifacts track
162	provenance (e.g., task files do not set these on themselves).
163	
164	#### 3e. Wikilink Convention
165	
166	All frontmatter fields that reference other files use Obsidian
167	wikilinks: `"[[name]]"`. This includes `subtasks`, `parent`,
168	`task`, and `artifacts`. The CLI strips `[[...]]` when resolving
169	names, so both `"[[0047-implement-storage-replacement]]"` and
170	`0047-implement-storage-replacement` are accepted.
171	
172	### 4. Artifact Routing
173	
174	During task execution, agents store artifacts in the appropriate
175	`openstation/<category>/` directory. The routing table:
176	
177	| Artifact Type        | Destination              |
178	|----------------------|--------------------------|
179	| Task creation        | `openstation/tasks/`     |
180	| Researcher output    | `openstation/research/`  |
181	| Agent spec           | `openstation/agents/`    |
182	| Planning notes       | `openstation/notes/`     |
183	| Other agent output   | `openstation/specs/`     |
184	
185	Agents also record produced artifacts in the task's frontmatter
186	`artifacts` list using canonical paths (§ 3c) and should set
187	provenance fields on the artifact itself (§ 3d).
188	
189	### 5. Sub-task Storage
190	
191	Sub-tasks are full tasks with their own canonical file in
192	`openstation/tasks/`, linked to a parent through frontmatter.
193	They differ from top-level tasks in two ways:
194	
195	1. **Parent field.** The sub-task's frontmatter sets
196	   `parent: "[[<parent-task-name>]]"` (§ 3b).
197	2. **Subtasks field.** The parent's frontmatter lists the
198	   sub-task in its `subtasks` field as a wikilink (§ 3a).
199	
200	#### Creating a sub-task
201	
202	1. Create canonical file: `openstation/tasks/MMMM-sub-slug.md`.
203	2. Set `parent: "[[<parent-task-name>]]"` in sub-task frontmatter.
204	3. Add `"[[MMMM-sub-slug]]"` to the parent's `subtasks`
205	   frontmatter field.
206	4. Add an entry to the parent's `## Subtasks` body section.
207	
208	#### Blocking rule
209	
210	All sub-tasks must reach `done` before the parent can proceed
211	to `review`.
212	
213	#### Status tracking
214	
215	Each sub-task tracks its own status in its frontmatter,
216	following the same transitions as any task.
217	
218	#### Discovery
219	
220	Sub-tasks are discovered through the parent's `subtasks`
221	frontmatter field, or by querying all tasks with a given
222	`parent` value.
223	
224	### 6. Install-time Layout
225	
226	When installed into a target project via `openstation init`, the
227	vault uses two directories:
228	
229	```
230	target-project/
231	├── openstation/                   — User-facing artifacts (source of truth)
232	│   ├── tasks/
233	│   ├── agents/
234	│   ├── research/
235	│   ├── specs/
236	│   └── logs/
237	├── .openstation/                  — Framework plumbing (hidden)
238	│   ├── docs/                    — lifecycle.md, task.spec.md
239	│   ├── agents/                  — Discovery symlinks → ../../openstation/agents/
240	│   ├── skills/                  — Agent skills (openstation-execute)
241	│   ├── commands/                — Slash commands
242	│   ├── templates/               — Settings templates
243	│   └── openstation.yaml         — Project settings
244	├── .claude/
245	│   ├── commands → ../.openstation/commands
246	│   ├── agents  → ../.openstation/agents
247	│   ├── skills  → ../.openstation/skills
248	│   └── settings.json            — Claude Code settings
249	└── CLAUDE.md                    — Contains managed openstation section
250	```
251	
252	**Claude Code integration** is achieved through three directory
253	symlinks in `.claude/` that point into `.openstation/`:
254	
255	| `.claude/` entry  | Target                          | Purpose                  |
256	|-------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------|
257	| `commands/`       | `../.openstation/commands`      | Slash command discovery   |
258	| `agents/`         | `../.openstation/agents`        | `--agent` resolution     |
259	| `skills/`         | `../.openstation/skills`        | Skill loading            |
260	
261	The installer also:
262	
263	- Places `.gitkeep` files in empty content directories.
264	- Deploys pre-tool-use hooks (`validate-write-path.sh`,
265	  `block-destructive-git.sh`) and registers them in
266	  `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code settings, not Open Station settings).
267	- Injects a managed `<!-- openstation:start -->` …
268	  `<!-- openstation:end -->` section into `CLAUDE.md`.
269	- Copies example agent specs to `openstation/agents/` (skippable
270	  with `--no-agents`) and creates their discovery symlinks.
271	
272	### 7. Design Rationale
273	
274	**Canonical paths are stable.** Task files in `openstation/tasks/`
275	never move or rename. Any reference to
276	`openstation/tasks/NNNN-slug.md` remains valid across all lifecycle
277	stages.
278	
279	**Flat `openstation/tasks/` over nested.** All task files are
280	siblings under `openstation/tasks/` rather than nested by status
281	or parent. This keeps:
282	
283	- Task IDs globally unique and easily scannable (`ls openstation/tasks/`).
284	- No deep nesting that obscures the task list.
285	
286	**Symlink elimination.** Only discovery symlinks remain (for
287	Claude Code `--agent` resolution). All other relationships —
288	parent/child, task/artifact provenance — are encoded in YAML
289	frontmatter. This eliminates:
290	
291	- State-split bugs (symlink says one thing, frontmatter another).
292	- Obsidian incompatibility (intra-vault symlinks violate
293	  Obsidian's disjoint-folder rule).
294	- Extra git diffs from symlink create/delete on transitions.
295	
296	**Frontmatter as single source of truth.** Task lifecycle state,
297	relationships, and artifact provenance live exclusively in YAML
298	frontmatter fields. There is no secondary representation to keep

302	Markdown files with YAML frontmatter are both human-readable and
303	machine-parseable. This means:
304

307	- Git-native — all state is versioned, diffable, and mergeable.
